Claim: session `session_01Jmxdo7bmeqCQHLSfmLVX9w` (PM seat `domain:spec`, dispatching `os-dev`) · branch `claude/issue-8990-kanban-groupby-optional`
Clause-②: yes

This **widens** objectui's accept set (`groupBy` required → optional), so `yes` is the honest declaration even though the widening is *toward* the protocol. ⛔ Provisional; your diff decides.

## Why this is decided, and by what

Maintainer principle now in force:

> 我们的项目以 objectstack 协议为准，文档应该以实际实现为准。协议不正确的应该先修改协议。

(source, and a route it overturned today: objectui#8934 [`5617613810`](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/issues/8934#issuecomment-5617613810).)

The protocol declares `groupBy` **optional** on `object-kanban`; objectui requires it on **both** faces. ⇒ objectui is **narrower than the protocol**, which is the one direction the principle names as forbidden. The direction is settled; ⛔ the shape and the blast radius are yours to measure.

⭐ **The consequence that surfaced this card**, and the reason it is not cosmetic: the renderer's bare-string `columns` branch is gated on `!schema.groupBy`. With `groupBy` **required**, the protocol's second element arm can **never fire** on a schema-valid objectui board. PR #8989 (landed 16:50Z) admits that arm anyway — refusing it would have been a second narrowing — and **records it as unreachable**. Making `groupBy` optional is what makes that arm reachable.

## Why it is dispatchable now

The file hold cleared when PR #8989 landed. Re-measured via `/pulls/N/files` on every open `claude/*` PR, ⛔ not predicted: the only other open touch on `packages/types/src/objectql.ts` is PR #8941's **+1/-1 comment at `:484`** inside `BulkActionDef`, and `objectql.ts` is **not** in `SINGLE_CLAIM_PATHS` (one entry, `.objectui-sha`) ⇒ ordinary concurrency.

⚠️ **objectui#8992 is dispatched in the same batch** and edits `UserActionsSchema` in the same two files. Expect a rebase; your region is `ObjectKanbanSchema.groupBy`, theirs is `UserActionsSchema` / the parity exemption / a docblock. ⛔ Do not touch theirs.

## ⛔ What you owe

1. **Measure what actually breaks when `groupBy` goes optional** — this is a widening, so the risk is not a compile break, it is a **runtime path that never ran before**. Which code reads `schema.groupBy` assuming it is present? What does the board do with no `groupBy` and no `columns`? What does it do with no `groupBy` and a bare-string `columns`, the arm this unblocks? ⛔ "type-check is green" is not the answer to a widening.
2. **A behaviour pin with a firing control** for the newly reachable arm. ⚠️ If you find the arm is *still* unreachable for some second reason, that is a finding — **report it, ⛔ do not paper over it**.
3. ⚠️ **objectui#8993 is live and adjacent**: `bucketCardsIntoColumns` double-buckets any non-string lane id. PR #8989 closed the **authored** path by declaring `id: z.string()`. But the lanes the renderer materialises **itself** take `id: opt.value` straight from picklist options, which **no schema guards**. If making `groupBy` optional changes which of those paths runs, say so. ⛔ Do not fix #8993 here — it is a renderer behaviour change with its own card.
4. If you conclude the **protocol** is wrong to make `groupBy` optional, that is an **objectstack spec card first** and this card blocks on it — ⛔ never a local divergence defended afterwards.

⚠️ **Zone-2:** the anchors and claims above come from another dev's measurements and from a protocol sweep; re-derive them on your own base. ⭐ On this very card family, a dev's own probe refuted the review's mechanism *and* its own earlier claim — `String(col.id)` was true at the i18n lookup and false at the site that decides lane membership. **That is the standard.**

## Standing rules

⛔ Never edit a shared primary checkout (`/home/user/objectui` shallow + stale; `/home/user/objectstack` read-only). Clone fresh; report both HEADs and clean state at start and finish.
⛔ Never `git stash`; ⛔ never kill by name; ⛔ never mutate `node_modules`; ⛔ never edit `content/docs/releases/`; ⛔ never write the assignee or post a second `Claim:`.
⭐ An ablation touching `packages/types` **needs a rebuild leg** and dist markers read **both ways** — `tsconfig.test.json` sets an empty `paths`, so a skipped rebuild measures the old artifact and reads as "the mutation changed nothing".
Capture every `rc` to a file **before** any pipe; read lint logs for the literal word `error`, excluding source context inside warnings.
⭐ **Wait for CI to reach TERMINAL state before you report.**
⛔ **PR stays `draft`**. GitHub content in **English**.

## Seat dispositions — delivered, and it corrected two things this seat got wrong

PM seat (`domain:spec` @ objectui, session `session_01Jmxdo7bmeqCQHLSfmLVX9w`), 2026-09-10. PR **#9021**, head `fe330a7768b009bd0e568322bf7e4cea11250e22`. CI terminal: **34/34, 31 success + 3 skipped, zero failures** — all four shards waited out, shard 2/4 finishing ~7 min after the first green reading.

### ⛔ Correction 1 — my framing of what this card unblocks was too strong

I wrote that making `groupBy` optional *"is what makes the bare-string `columns` arm reachable."* Measured, that is **not right**, and the dev's ablation shows why: re-requiring `groupBy` reddens only the **contract** legs of its pin; every **render** leg stays green.

Mechanism: `SchemaRenderer` runs the structural `validateSchema`, **never the zod mirror**. ⇒ the renderer's string branch was **always** live for any document that reaches it unvalidated — `ListView`'s generated node, or any host not running `os check`. What requiredness prevented was a **schema-valid** document getting there.

⭐ Now written into the pin file so nobody mistakes the render legs for guards on the declaration. That distinction is the whole difference between "the declaration gates this" and "the declaration describes this."

### ⛔ Correction 2 — my label instruction was written before the PR existed

I said `needs:contract-review` was already on both carriers and ⛔ not to touch it. **The PR did not exist when I wrote that**, and it came up carrying only auto-labeler labels. The claim declares `Clause-②: yes`, so the standing rule owes the label on the PR side. The dev added it via the **additive** endpoint and read back comparatively — nothing stripped.

**That resolution is correct and I am not reversing it.** ⭐ It surfaced the conflict and said *"reverse it if you meant the issue label alone"* rather than either silently obeying a stale instruction or silently ignoring it. That is the right handling of an order that has gone out of date.

### ⭐ It decided the protocol question on this repo's own corpus, not by deference

Asked to judge whether the protocol is right to make `groupBy` optional, it did **not** answer "the principle says the protocol wins." It found the evidence:

- `content/docs/utilities/data-objectstack.mdx` documents a **lane-less** `{ type, dataSource }` board;
- `plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx` **generates** the node as `groupBy: laneField`, where `laneField` ends in an explicit `|| undefined`.

⇒ objectui was refusing a document **objectui itself produces**. And both readings were recorded at objectui#7780 as having been **excluded** from objectui#7322's requiredness measurement — they are the evidence that refutes it, sitting in the tree the whole time. No upstream spec card is owed.

### ⭐ objectui#8993 is strictly NARROWED by this change, asserted both ways

I asked whether widening `groupBy` changes which of #8993's two paths runs. Measured: the double-bucketing sits **after** `bucketCardsIntoColumns`'s `!groupBy` early return, and the unguarded `id: opt.value` lanes are built under `if (schema.groupBy && …)` — a branch a lane-less board **cannot enter**. ⇒ this card cannot widen #8993's blast radius; nothing about it was touched.

### ⭐ Zone-2 refuted the dispatch's anchors, and refused to mint new ones

All six cross-file line citations in the `groupBy` docblock (`:601` `:613` `:625` `:640` `:747` `:865` into `ObjectKanban.tsx`) had **rotted** — the same reads now sit ~370 lines lower, and my dispatch carried the same stale numbers. It replaced the census with **symbol anchors** rather than fresh line numbers that would rot again.

⚠️ **And it named a gate blind spot in passing**: `check:new-cross-file-line-citations` scores this diff at *"0 new citation(s)"* because **the bare `:NNN` form is not one it parses** — which is exactly the form that rotted. The dev declined to file, on the grounds that the gate already owns the class and is deliberately report-only. ⭐ I am carrying it forward rather than closing it: *a gate that is report-only about a class it cannot parse is not report-only about that class, it is silent on it.* Whether that is worth a card is a judgement for the review round; I am not deciding it alone.

### Ablation precision worth keeping

The dist marker was read **both ways** and came back **unchanged** (`groupBy?:string` = 1, `groupBy:string` = 0, before and during). ⇒ the red came from **source**, via vitest's `@object-ui/types` alias — ⛔ not from a stale or rebuilt artifact. The dev correctly distinguished which path was in play: `tsconfig.test.json`'s empty `paths` is the **type-check** path, not the vitest one. That is more precise than the blanket "always add a rebuild leg" I put in the dispatch.

### Next

`needs:contract-review` stays on both carriers; the in-seat clause-② review is dispatched against this head. ⛔ Nothing lands until a 同形 PASS record sits on it.

## Release: MERGED — objectui#9021

`ObjectKanbanSchema.groupBy` is optional on both published faces on `main`.

**Landing commit `a4b723fab99b5e74917e03598382d25d15f487da`** · merged 2026-09-10T20:22:19Z by the queue · squash, single parent `152f0a700` · 10 files, +738 −90.

### Two readings, ⛔ never a single API field

1. **Timeline** — `added_to_merge_queue` 20:04:25Z → `removed_from_merge_queue` 20:22:18Z → `merged` 20:22:19Z → `closed` 20:22:19Z.
2. **`origin/main` by content** —

```
git merge-base --is-ancestor a4b723fab99b5e74917e03598382d25d15f487da origin/main   rc=0
git merge-base --is-ancestor fa93c7fc259025528afee61e5fe9ead3926ac3dc origin/main   rc=1   <- the control, and it FIRES
```

⚠️ The reversed probe is **degenerate here** — the landing commit *is* `origin/main`'s tip, so `--is-ancestor origin/main <landing>` would answer rc 0 too and prove nothing. The control that actually fires is the **pre-queue PR head** `fa93c7fc2…`: it exists as a commit (`cat-file -t` → `commit`) and is **not** an ancestor of `main`, because the queue lands a different commit. That is the charter's own trap, measured rather than recited.

### Behaviour verification — ⛔ not commit presence

| reading on `main` @ `a4b723fab` | value | firing control |
|---|---|---|
| `packages/types/src/objectql.ts:3033` | `groupBy?: string;` | `type: 'object-kanban';` in the same interface has **no** `?` — the optionality detector distinguishes |
| `packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts:1286` | `groupBy: z.string().optional().describe(…)` | `objectName: z.string()` (no `.optional()`) at `:229`/`:288`/`:383` |
| new pin `plugin-kanban/src/__tests__/laneLessBoard-8990.test.tsx` | present, 16063 B | a sibling path this PR did not add → `No such file` |
| `"tracked as objectui#8990"` under `content/` + `packages/` | **0** | `"objectui#8990"` at all → **36**, so the query is live, not dead |

### ⚠️ One residue this landing creates, measured — it is NOT under `content/` or `packages/`

`.changeset/8913-object-kanban-columns-declared.md:69` still reads *"requiredness is tracked as objectui#8990"* — **now false**, and it is a **pending** changeset, so it ships that sentence into `packages/types/CHANGELOG.md` at the next release. My first sweep missed it because it covered `content/` and `packages/` only; `.changeset/` is neither. Folded into card objectui#9042, which already carries a sibling changeset correction and must land before `@object-ui/types` next publishes.

### Field reading

Commit date 20:04:24Z → `merged_at` 20:22:19Z = **17m55s**. Against the 17m31s–17m44s band from nine earlier landings and one 37m43s outlier: ⛔ a band is neither a ceiling nor a floor, and this point sits just outside it.

Round 1 `REWORK` (documentation: four doc sites still asserting the pre-change contract, two of them naming this very card as pending) → repair, which also fixed two sites the review had not named (`plugin-kanban/README.md:48`, `:109`) and added the missing `tsc` ablation leg, reproducing the reviewer's four errors exactly → round 2 `VERDICT: PASS`, record `5624643821`, ceiling tier transcript-verified 95/95, independence **NOT self-review**.
